# Information Architecture

## Procedure
1. Inventory authorized content, user tasks, current navigation, terminology, and access boundaries. Keep artifacts in approved product-owned storage.
2. Group information by task and evidenced mental models rather than internal organization alone. Identify duplicates, missing labels, and ambiguous routes.
3. Define hierarchy, labels, search/navigation entry points, current-location cues, and routes back to the task. Preserve authorization boundaries across navigation.
4. Request authorized card-sorting or tree-testing through VOC where useful. Do not claim research occurred without participant records; use heuristic findings as hypotheses.
5. Implement only approved changes and test deep links, back navigation, keyboard access, empty searches, and mobile navigation. Compare findability against the stated task criteria.

## Completion Checks
Tasks map to navigable paths with clear labels and location cues. No intoxication-based tests or stereotyped proxies substitute for representative, consented research.

Original procedure informed by item 6 of [UX Playbook's UX skills article](https://uxplaybook.org/articles/top-skills-every-ux-designer-needs), accessed October 11, 2026.
